feat.title: Your {{name}} feat asks for a few choices
feat.whyTitle: Where do these choices come from?
feat.why: These choices come from a feat you gained: they are part of the same package, but filling them in is up to you.

level.epicWhy: At level 19, an epic boon crowns your progression.
level.asiWhy: At this level, you can raise your ability scores or take a feat. The improvement is the safe choice; a feat brings a new ability.

skills.title_one: Which skill are you proficient in?
skills.title_other: Which {{count}} skills are you proficient in?
skills.why: A proficient skill adds your proficiency bonus to every check it covers. Take the ones that fit how you play: talking, searching, surviving, sneaking…

tool.why: Proficiency with a tool adds your proficiency bonus when you use it: playing an instrument, forging, picking a lock…

fighting-style.title: What is your fighting style?
fighting-style.why: A permanent bonus that shapes the way you fight. Archery for the bow, Defense to take hits, Dueling or Great Weapon Fighting depending on the weapon you plan to carry.

subclass.title: {{label}}: your choice
subclass.why: At level 3, your class specialises. The subclass adds its own features at the following levels.

equipment.title: What equipment do you set out with?
equipment.why: The pack equips you right away and leaves a little gold. Gold alone lets you buy everything yourself at the Equipment step: more freedom, more time.

lineage.title: {{label}}: your choice
lineage.why: This choice specifies what your species gives you: spells, resistance, speed or vision depending on the option.

size.title: What is your size?
size.whyTitle: Small or Medium, what's the difference?
size.why: Mostly a matter of looks: the rules treat a Small and a Medium creature almost the same way.

skill.title: Which extra skill?
skill.whyTitle: Where does this skill come from?
skill.why: A trait of your species makes you proficient in an extra skill.

spell-ability.title: Which ability do you cast your species spells with?
spell-ability.why: It sets the attack bonus and the DC of those spells. Take your best mental ability, usually your class's.

origin-feat.title: Which origin feat do you take?
origin-feat.why: An origin feat is a small starting talent. If it asks for choices (skills, spells…), they come at the next sub-step.

spells.title: Which spells do you take along?
spells.lead: Fill both hands: cantrips first, then prepared spells.
spells.why: Cantrips are cast at will. Prepared spells use up a slot: take enough to heal, protect or strike depending on your role in the group. You can change them later from the sheet.

masteries.title: Which weapons have you truly mastered?
masteries.lead: You use the mastery property of these weapons on every attack.
masteries.whyTitle: What is a weapon mastery for?
masteries.why: A mastery adds an effect to every hit with the weapon: topple, slow, push… Take the ones you plan to carry: the weapons in your pack head the list. You can change them from the sheet.

expertise.title: Which skills do you excel at?
expertise.lead: Your proficiency bonus counts double for these skills.
expertise.why: Only the skills you are already proficient in are offered: your class's, then your species' and background's once chosen. Take the ones that make your name in the group: sneaking, convincing, spotting…

hit-points.title: How many hit points do you gain each level?
hit-points.lead: Beyond level 1, each level adds a hit die: take the average, or roll it.
hit-points.why: The average is safe. The roll may do better… or worse. Your GM may have a preference: some tables require one or the other.

impact.title: What this change removes and brings
impact.lead: Nothing changes on the sheet until you apply the changes.
impact.whyTitle: What happens to my old choices?
impact.why: A new origin or a new class takes its traits, its features and what it had you choose with it. The next screens only ask the new questions.

class.title: Which class do you want to play?

background.title: What life did you lead before adventuring?

identity.title: What is your character called?
identity.lead: The starting level decides the features and choices that follow.
identity.why: Most campaigns start at level 1. Beyond that, the subclass (level 3) and level feats (4, 8…) are added to the sub-steps.

features.title: What your {{class}} can do
features.lead: Nothing to choose here: these are the features gained up to level {{level}}.
features.why: These features will appear on the sheet, with their uses per rest.

traits.title: What your species gives you
traits.lead: Nothing to choose here: your traits apply as they are.
traits.why: Species traits don't depend on level, except lineage spells, which arrive at levels 3 and 5.

alignment.title: What is your moral compass?
alignment.lead: Alignment sums up in two words how your character usually acts.
alignment.why: It has no effect in play: it's a landmark for you and your GM. A character can change over a campaign.

languages.title: Which languages do you speak?
languages.lead: You already speak the languages you gained; add {{count}} more.
languages.why: Standard languages come up often; rare languages are precious in some campaigns. Ask your GM where the adventure takes place.

lore.title: Where does your character come from?
lore.lead: Optional: a few lines are enough to give the GM something to work with.
lore.why: Think about what links your past as a {{background}} to the adventure: a bond, a debt, a secret, a goal.

method.title: How do you determine your scores?
method.lead: The four methods give six scores; they differ in how much chance and freedom they leave.
method.why: The standard array is the simplest and most balanced. Point buy lets you fine-tune. Dice give more uneven characters. Ask your GM what they prefer.

values.title: Place your six scores
values.lead: Put your best scores in {{abilities}}: that's what your class needs most.
values.whyTitle: Where to put the best scores?
values.why: Put the highest in your class's primary ability: it sets your attacks or your spells. “Suggested” proposes a typical spread, which you don't have to follow.

bonus.title: Where do your background's bonuses go?
bonus.lead: {{background}}: +2 and +1, or +1 to three abilities, among {{abilities}}.
bonus.why: In 2024, the background, not the species, gives the ability score bonuses. Boosting your primary ability almost always pays off.

recap.title: Your character by the numbers
recap.lead: Everything that follows from your scores, your class and your species.
recap.whyTitle: What if I change my mind?
recap.why: You can go back to any sub-step from the left panel: everything is recalculated.

kit.title: What you already carry
kit.lead: Your class and background packs, and the gold you have left.
kit.whyTitle: What if I only took gold?
kit.why: If you took gold rather than a pack, it all happens at the next sub-step. You can still change pack from the Class and Background steps.

shop.title: Fill up your bag
shop.lead: Only adventuring gear is for sale: weapons and armor come from the class pack.
shop.why: Rope, torches, rations, a healing potion: the classics that save a first session. Going over your purse is allowed, your GM will decide.

review.title: Your character is almost ready
review.lead: Here is the sheet as it will be saved. Each block has a button to go back to the right sub-step.

wildShape.title: Which beasts can you turn into?
wildShape.lead: Tick the forms your druid knows.
wildShape.why: Wild Shape only uses known forms: their number and highest CR grow at levels 4 and 8, and flight comes at level 8. In play, you can swap a form after a long rest, from the sheet.

skill-swap.title: A skill taken twice
skill-swap.why: When two sources give the same skill, the second would be wasted: the rules let you pick another one, among those you are not proficient in yet.

issues.name: Give your character a name.
issues.expertiseProficient: Expertise only applies to a skill you are proficient in.
issues.hitPoints_one: Choose how you gain your hit points.
issues.hitPoints_other: Choose the hit points of {{count}} levels.

rail.heading: Character creation
rail.guestNote: Without an account, the creation stays on this device

class.label: Class
class.title: Step 1: Class
class.description: Your class decides your hit points, your proficiencies and what you can do in combat.

species.label: Species
species.title: Step 2: Species
species.description: Your species sets your size, your speed and your traits. It gives no ability score bonus in 2024.

background.label: Background
background.title: Step 3: Background
background.description: Your background brings two skills, a tool proficiency, an origin feat and your ability score bonuses.

abilities.label: Ability scores
abilities.title: Step 4: Ability scores
abilities.description: Spread your six scores, then add your background's bonuses. HP, proficiency and hit die follow from them.

shop.label: Equipment
shop.title: Step 5: Equipment
shop.description: Take stock of your pack, top it up at the shop, then review the sheet.

shell.pointBuyRange: Point buy: each score must stay between 8 and 15.
shell.guestHandOff: Create an account or sign in: your character is waiting for you here.
shell.choiceLeft: One choice is still to be made before confirming.
shell.confirmText: Here is the sheet before and after. Removed items disappear when you save.

shop.overspent: You are over your purse by {{amount}}. You can carry on — your GM will decide.
shop.noGold: Your starting pack leaves no gold. Take the “gold” option again at steps 1 or 3 to buy things yourself.

impactStep.ack_one: Understood: this item will be removed when I apply the changes. Nothing moves before that.
impactStep.ack_other: Understood: these {{count}} items will be removed when I apply the changes. Nothing moves before that.
impactStep.ackNone: Understood: the sheet will change when I apply the changes. Nothing moves before that.

spells.alwaysHint: Granted by a feature, the species or an invocation: they don't count towards your hands.
spells.grantedBy: Granted by {{sources}}: always prepared, outside the count, and cannot be removed.

fixed.name: Character name
fixed.nameHint: . A name, a nickname, a title: you can change it later.
fixed.levelOne: Level 1: no extra choices, the simplest way to start.
fixed.lorePlaceholder: Where do they come from, what drives them…
fixed.loreLater: No rush: you can write or rework this story later, from the character sheet.

kit.goldOnly: Gold only: everything is bought at the next sub-step.

review.readyHint: Everything is filled in. Review, then confirm.
review.noLore: Not written yet: optional, but your GM will appreciate it.
review.noPreview: The sheet shows here once the six ability scores are set.

hints.standardArray: 15, 14, 13, 12, 10 and 8 to place. Balanced, no surprises.
hints.pointBuy: {{budget}} points to spread between 8 and 15. The most control.
hints.roll: 4d6 six times, keep the three best dice. Chance and surprises.
hints.manual: You copy scores obtained elsewhere: at the table, on a paper sheet.

abilities.trayDone: All the tokens are placed. Click an ability to take its token back.
abilities.trayIdle: Click a token then an ability, or drag it.
abilities.fillFirst: Fill in your six scores first.

visual.shopLater: You will go shopping at the Equipment step.
visual.alreadyClass: This is already your {{ofClass}} spellcasting ability: only one score to raise.

shell2.confirmChange: Tick the box to confirm this change.

gains.title: At level {{level}}, {{name}} gains…
gains.lead: Nothing to choose here: what is chosen comes on the next screens.
gains.why: The listed features are added to the sheet as they are. Hit points are settled on the next screen.

levelUp.hitPointsTitle: How many hit points do you gain at level {{level}}?

expertise.title: Which skills do you excel at?
expertise.lead: Your proficiency bonus counts double for these skills.
expertise.why: Take the skills you use most: the ones that make your name in the group.

masteries.title: Which extra weapon do you master?
masteries.lead: You use the mastery property of one more weapon.
masteries.whyTitle: What is a weapon mastery for?
masteries.why: A mastery adds an effect to every hit with the weapon: topple, slow, push… Take the one you carry most often.

spells.title: Which spells do you prepare now?
spells.lead: Fill up your hands if the level gives more. It's also the time to swap some.
spells.why: Upcast a spell you missed, or replace the one you never cast. Always-prepared spells don't count.

review.title: Your character at level {{level}}
review.lead: Before and after, recalculated by the rules engine.
review.why: Once confirmed, the sheet moves to the new level. You can still correct a choice from the sheet.

levelUp.choiceLeft: One choice is still to be made before confirming.
levelUp.heading: Level up
levelUp.noFeature: No new feature at this level.
